findings.current: A feeling that belongs not only to a person, but to a place or an object, too.
findings.defect: The source describes this as a distinctive, inherent feeling. The translation says it belongs to those things but drops that defining quality.
findings.rationale: 고유한 느낌 means a unique or inherent feeling; the accepted baseline preserved this with “distinctive.”
findings.replacement: A distinctive feeling that belongs not only to a person, but to a place or an object, too.

findings.current: I turned and met the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s gaze. He had been staring at me.
findings.defect: The source’s image of a gaze fixed intently on the narrator is weakened; the translation instead says he had been staring at the narrator, changing the direction of his attention.
findings.rationale: The source says he had been looking this way (이쪽을 빤히 바라보고 있던), not specifically staring at the narrator before they met eyes.
findings.replacement: I turned and met the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s gaze. He had been staring intently in my direction.

findings.current: For some reason, the closer he came, the more his son’s eyes darkened.
findings.defect: “Darkened” changes the source’s image of the son’s eyes sinking deeply.
findings.rationale: 깊게 가라앉아가는 describes the eyes sinking deeper, an image also preserved in the accepted baseline; it does not say they darkened.
findings.replacement: For some reason, the closer his father came, the more deeply his son’s eyes sank.

findings.current: I only meant that, with this sense of danger hanging over them, the civilians would feel an even greater urgency to protect themselves. That, too, could be a way to save their lives.
findings.defect: “Urgency to protect themselves” adds a specific response that the source does not state.
findings.rationale: The source says they would feel a greater sense of crisis (더욱 큰 위기감), not specifically an urgency to take protective action.
findings.replacement: I only meant that, with these warning signs around them, the civilians would feel an even greater sense of danger. That, too, could be a way to save their lives.

findings.current: Too late to pretend I hadn’t noticed. I glanced at Jeok Cheongang, who was still frowning at Sima Gong. He nodded.
findings.defect: The first sentence repeats the preceding paragraph’s statement that it was too late to pretend not to notice the gaze.
findings.rationale: The source gives this beat once before the narrator glances at Jeok Cheongang and receives his nod; the repeated sentence adds emphasis absent from the source.
findings.replacement: I glanced at Jeok Cheongang, who was still frowning at Sima Gong. He nodded.

summary: The chapter is broadly faithful, but several small source details were altered or added.
